results.title: How will your Auditor use Vanta? | Vanta Help Center
results.content: How will your Auditor use Vanta? # How will your Auditor use Vanta? Vanta automates evidence collection and cross-maps controls across over 35 frameworks, streamlining the compliance process. The customer and auditor collaborate closely to ensure all compliance controls are met with the required evidence and tests. Audits occur during a specific duration, as determined by the auditor and customer. The customer will indicate the audit period in Vanta, when auditors will have access to evidence and are expected to complete their assessment. Auditors have limited access to the Vanta instance, depending on what the customer has decided to share. The Evidence page is a repository for evidence that supports and is mapped to a customer's controls. Auditors will use this page to review ready-for-audit evidence and assess and approve evidence. If an auditor wants to add custom audit requests, they can do so from this page. Auditors can directly communicate with customers by adding comments to individual pieces of evidence. From this page, the auditor will see automated tests and documents assigned to each control for testing purposes. * Auditors can map/re-map evidence to controls. * In this view, auditors review evidence for a particular control and can accept, flag, or mark it as not required. * Evidence in the auditor's instance can be a document, policy, or test. Auditors can also change the control status and comment on any evidence they review. This is where auditors can identify what integrations the customer has linked to Vanta, what resources are in scope for the audit, and a high-level overview of a particular integration. Auditors cannot change what is determined in scope, the customer manages this. Customers use Vanta to automate compliance by automating the collection of evidence needed to demonstrate adherence to standards like SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Auditors leverage a customer’s Vanta instance to conduct an unbiased evaluation of an organization’s security controls. Vanta automates numerous tests required for audits, streamlining evidence collection and ensuring continuous compliance through always-on automated testing. Some controls, however, will still necessitate manual document updates to provide auditors with sufficient evidence.

results.title: Adjudication: Overview, definition, and example - Cobrief
results.content: ### **What is adjudication?**. Adjudication is the legal process of resolving a dispute or legal matter by a court, tribunal, or other authorized body. Adjudication is important because it provides a structured, formal means of resolving disputes in a fair and orderly manner. In many cases, adjudication results in legally binding decisions that must be followed by the parties involved. In another example, two parties involved in a construction contract dispute may submit their case to an arbitrator for adjudication. ### **An example of an adjudication clause**. > *“In the event of a dispute arising under this Agreement, the Parties agree to submit the matter to adjudication by [name of the adjudicator or arbitration panel]. Adjudication is a fundamental process in the legal system, allowing disputes to be resolved in a formal, structured, and impartial manner. Whether through a court, tribunal, or arbitration panel, adjudication ensures that parties receive a fair hearing and a legally enforceable decision.

results.title: Improvement, OFIs, and Auditor Independence - The Auditor
results.content: Instead of relying on their systems to help them identify improvement opportunities, auditees expect their auditors to report them. This has already started with internal auditors, many of whom are asked to change the definition of audit itself from: “Systematic, independent, and documented process for obtaining audit evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which audit criteria are fulfilled (per ISO 19011).” To: “Systematic and documented process for obtaining audit evidence and suggesting better ways of fulfilling audit criteria (per management preference).”. #### **Improvement, OFIs, and auditor independence: Removing the fear of nonconformity reports**. Auditors add value by delivering carefully worded nonconformity when the evidence shows that the system has failed to help the users to meet requirements. #### **Improvement, OFIs, and auditor independence: Why do we nanny the systems we audit?**. Auditors should stop propping up weak systems with their OFIs. Instead, we should be investigating why the systems we audit are failing to inform system users of needed improvement. They should make it clear that their auditors will collect and evaluate evidence of the commitment of the organization’s leaders to the development, use, and improvement of its process-based risk management systems. Managers who understand these concepts won’t accept OFIs from auditors because they will be more concerned about why their system failed and helping their employees other opportunities for improvement. When the registrar, the auditor, and the auditee create this kind of improvement-focused environment, they welcome the reporting of genuine system weaknesses as nonconformity statements that require corrective action. Conversely, after dysfunctional audits employees talk about how the auditor failed to report valid system weaknesses while their managers celebrate a lack of reported nonconformities. Auditors add value by invoking corrective actions that strengthen the system when it’s failing to help its users to meet requirements and secure needed improvement. He designs and runs lively advanced auditing workshops for accredited registrars and develops process-based management systems that add value faster and prevent loss sooner while conforming to any number of system standards using a continual improvement methodology. *Tags: improvement, auditor independence, OFIs, value-added audits.*.

results.title: PwC auditor cancels rego amid ASIC dispute | Accountants Daily
results.content: Sign up to our Newsletter. ### MENU. # PwC auditor cancels rego amid ASIC dispute. ASIC accepted the request of a big four firm partner to cancel his registration as a registered company auditor after his retirement, which follows a dispute between the two parties. 27 November 2017 • By Reporter • 4 minutes read. PwC partner Stephen James Bourke was the lead auditor for the audit of the financial report of Vocation Limited for the year ended 30 June 2014. The big four firm was named as a defendant in the class action brought against failed education and training company Vocation Limited, being accused of misleading or deceptive conduct over its audits of Vocation’s 2014 financial statements. ASIC believes that Mr Bourke should have gathered further audit evidence post-balance date and prior to signing the audit opinion concerning Vocation's dispute with the Victorian Department of Education and Early Childhood Development. In the corporate regulator’s view, Mr Bourke should have obtained this further evidence in connection with the recognition and recoverability at year-end of a material accrued revenue asset and consideration of any possible impact on goodwill. Accordingly, ASIC believes that Mr Bourke did not carry out, or perform adequately or properly the duties of an auditor in this respect. Mr Bourke denies this is the case and says he took all appropriate steps. A spokesperson from PwC told Accountants Daily that it has no further comment, and that the firm, through Mr Bourke, denies the matters raised by ASIC. You’re out of free articles for this month.
